protocol.instrument_name: NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis (Community Pharmacy Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis Service Practice Standard)
protocol.instrument_version: NSW Health Authority dated 25 February 2026; approved 25 February 2026
protocol.legal_basis: NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026); pharmacists must hold general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law and have successfully completed the training requirements detailed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026). Approved Medicines are listed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026).
protocol.supervision_model: approved pharmacist - appropriately trained approved pharmacists manage eligible patients as part of the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026); pharmacists must exercise professional discretion and judgement when applying the Practice Standard
protocol.scope_summary: NSW Health practice standard for approved pharmacists managing eligible patients with allergic or nonallergic rhinitis in a community pharmacy: approved medicines (intranasal and eye drop formulations), assessment flowchart, consent, eligibility and red-flag referral criteria, general measures and pharmacotherapy, 4-week supply limit and follow-up review, documentation and communication requirements. Only management of allergic and nonallergic rhinitis is permitted under the Authority and this practice standard.

inclusion.text: Patients must be aged 6 years and older to be eligible for the service.

provenance.section_heading: G. PATIENT ELIGIBILITY AND REFERRAL CRITERIA

inclusion.text: Patients must be physically present in the pharmacy to be eligible for management.
Patients are required to have a consultation with an approved pharmacist before a medication can be supplied under the Authority.
To receive management for allergic and nonallergic rhinitis under this service, the patient must fulfill the eligibility requirements of the Practice Standard.
Informed clinical and financial consent must be obtained from the patient prior to providing care under this practice standard.
Patient presents to a participating approved pharmacist for management of allergic or nonallergic rhinitis.
The patient has no acute respiratory signs, red flags, or exclusions (checked in the flowchart against Section G).

Only management of allergic and nonallergic rhinitis is permitted under the Authority and this practice standard (aetiology classified as allergic, nonallergic, infectious, drug-induced and occupational; only allergic and nonallergic are in scope).

exclusion.text: The patient has any 'red flag' warning sign (see box above).

steps.description: Patient presents to a participating approved pharmacist for management of allergic or nonallergic rhinitis.
Is the patient >=6 years old? If No: 'Not eligible for management under the Authority and Practice Standard. Refer to GP.'
Does the patient have any acute respiratory signs, red flags, or exclusions? If Yes: 'Not eligible for management under the Authority and Practice Standard. Refer to Emergency Department or GP.'

gates.criterion: No acute respiratory signs, red flags or exclusions

steps.description: Conduct patient informed consent: Participation; Financial; Pharmacist communication with other health practitioners. If No: 'Not eligible for management under the Authority and Practice Standard. Refer to GP.'

gates.criterion: Informed consent obtained (participation, financial, communication with other health practitioners)

steps.description: Conduct patient history and clinical review including review of contraindications, precautions, drug interactions, pregnancy and lactation status.
Establish management plan.
Communicate agreed management plan with patient and patient's medical practitioner. Document all aspects of management plan.

Patient history should include: Age; Pregnancy and lactation status (if applicable); Onset, nature, duration, frequency, severity and pattern of respiratory symptoms; Signs and symptoms suggestive of systemic infection such as fever; Signs and symptoms of infectious rhinosinusitis including purulent nasal discharge or facial pain; Presence of asthma symptoms (acute exacerbations of asthma, any presentation of asthma in persons under 16 years of age, or a potential new presentation of asthma require an immediate referral to a medical practitioner and are beyond the scope of this practice standard); Other co-existing and underlying medical conditions including nasal polyps, other allergic diseases (e.g. atopic dermatitis); Family history of nasal polyps or allergic disease (including rhinitis); Triggering, aggravating and relieving factors; Emotional and social impacts of the condition; Current medication use; Medications used or trialled to treat symptoms, adherence and response, including use of nasal decongestants; Drug allergies and adverse drug reactions; Smoking and vaping status. The My Health Record should be reviewed where appropriate and available.

Physical examination of patient, with specific focus of the face, nose, throat, eyes and ears. Pharmacist must have an otoscope to complete a full examination. Assessment of vital signs. Signs of rhinitis may include: swollen, dark undereye area; accentuated lines or fold below the lower lids; transverse nasal crease; 'Allergic facies': highly arched palate, open mouth; enlarged/swollen, pale, boggy nasal mucosa with thick secretions; nasal polyps; cobblestone throat; mouth breathing; tympanic membrane retraction or serous fluid accumulation. Patients presenting with acute exacerbations of asthma, any presentation of asthma in persons under 16 years of age, or a potential new presentation of asthma require an immediate referral to a medical practitioner and are beyond the scope of this practice standard.

gates.criterion: Pharmacist has an otoscope to complete a full examination

steps.description: Differential of rhinitis type (allergic vs non-allergic) using the 'Symptoms and signs of rhinitis' table: allergic rhinitis symptoms occur after exposure to animals, pollen, dust or other environmental factors/allergens; non-allergic rhinitis symptoms occur without an identifiable trigger or exposure to allergens. 'Reported symptom improvement with second generation antihistamines is strongly suggestive of allergic rhinitis, as is a previous response to intranasal corticosteroids.' Accurate differentiation of the type of rhinitis is important to inform effective treatment.
All patients should be educated regarding allergen avoidance and minimising exposure to known/clinically obvious allergens and irritants if possible.

Pharmacotherapy as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Allergic rhinitis / Nonallergic rhinitis using Approved Medicines only: Fluticasone furoate (intranasal formulation); Olopatadine with mometasone (intranasal formulation); Olopatadine 0.1% (eye drops). 'Pharmacists must only supply formulations listed in the Authority.' 'Pharmacists can supply up to 4 weeks of therapy before referring patient to a medical practitioner.' 'Once symptoms have resolved, continue treatment with the minimum effective regimen, treatment can be used regularly or as required.'

gates.criterion: Only formulations listed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026) are supplied
Supply does not exceed 4 weeks of therapy before referring patient to a medical practitioner

steps.description: ALLERGIC RHINTIS specifications: 'Pharmacists must advise patients with allergic rhinitis who are being commenced on intranasal corticosteroids to expect symptom relief to occur within 1-2 weeks, and if this does not occur how to access follow-up care and review with a medical practitioner.' 'Oral and intranasal decongestants have no role in allergic rhinitis.' 'Montelukast (a leukotriene receptor antagonist) supply is not currently permitted under the Authority and this practice standard.' 'Supply of anti-inflammatory eye drops (e.g. ketorolac and corticosteroids) for allergic conjunctivitis ... are not permitted under this practice standard, and are for use under medical specialist advice only. Vasoconstrictor eye drops (e.g. naphazoline and tetryzoline) are not indicated for allergic conjunctivitis.' 'Pharmacist must refer to a medical practitioner for consideration of onward referral to a clinical immunology/allergy specialist to initiate allergen immunotherapy for allergic rhinitis.'

gates.criterion: No supply of Montelukast under this practice standard
No supply of anti-inflammatory eye drops (e.g. ketorolac and corticosteroids) under this practice standard
No supply of oral or intranasal decongestants for allergic rhinitis

steps.description: NONALLERGIC RHINITIS: 'In patients with nonallergic rhinitis caused by a clinically obvious irritant, minimise exposure to the irritant if possible.' 'Topical antihistamines and oral antihistamines are not indicated for nonallergic rhinitis.' 'Intranasal corticosteroids are the mainstay of treatment, with dosages being same as those used for allergic rhinitis.'

gates.criterion: No topical or oral antihistamines used for nonallergic rhinitis

steps.description: Comprehensive advice and counselling (including supporting written information when required) as per the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook, and other relevant references regarding: individual product and medicine use, including intranasal spray and eyedrop administration technique; how to manage adverse effects; when to seek further care and/or treatment from a medical practitioner.

The agreed management plan must be documented in the patient electronic clinical record and shared with members of the patient's multidisciplinary team, in accordance with the Authority. Where a patient has a My Health Record, the pharmacist must ensure the details of the supply are uploaded to My Health Record, unless requested otherwise by the patient.

If the patient's symptoms are mild and adequately managed with an oral or intranasal antihistamine after trialling a new treatment for 4 weeks, clinical review will generally not be required, and the patient may be advised to remain on the minimum effective dose.

gates.criterion: Symptoms are mild and adequately managed with an oral or intranasal antihistamine after trialling a new treatment for 4 weeks

steps.description: Clinical review is recommended 4 weeks after initiation of intranasal corticosteroids to assess for response to treatment, adherence to treatment, and if changes to the treatment plan are required (continue, modify, stop and/or refer).

gates.criterion: Intranasal corticosteroid initiated and 4 weeks elapsed

steps.description: If the condition does not improve or resolve after 4 weeks of optimal therapy, the patient should be advised to see a medical practitioner for review and further investigation. Also: 'The condition does not respond to optimal treatment after 4 weeks or worsens' requires referral to a medical practitioner and the patient is not eligible for the service.

gates.criterion: Condition does not improve or resolve after 4 weeks of optimal therapy, or worsens

steps.description: Patients must be referred to a medical practitioner if they meet any of the referral criteria: any 'red flag' warning sign; a clear diagnosis of allergic or nonallergic rhinitis cannot be made; signs or symptoms of systemic infection or infectious rhinosinusitis including facial pain, fever or purulent nasal discharge; aged under 6 years of age; acute exacerbation of asthma; other underlying or co-existing medical conditions that complicate treatment including sinusitis, nasal polyps, other structural abnormalities; taking a medicine prescribe by another health practitioner that can cause or exacerbate rhinitis; marked negative emotional or social effect; condition does not respond to optimal treatment after 4 weeks or worsens.

gates.criterion: Any of the Section G referral criteria met

Patients who meet any of the referral criteria below are not eligible for this service and must be referred to their regular medical practitioner or health service, or in instances of urgent care to the Emergency Department.

conditions: If the treating pharmacist becomes aware of an uncommon, unexpected or serious adverse event following treatment with an Approved Medicine, this should be reported to the Therapeutic Goods Administration. Additionally, you must notify the patient's usual medical practitioner (if they have one).
Where a patient has a My Health Record, the pharmacist must ensure the details of the supply are uploaded to My Health Record, unless requested otherwise by the patient.

open_questions.topic: Flowchart box order reconstructed from diagram layout
open_questions.observed: Section D flowchart text is interleaved in the extraction, e.g. 'Is the patient >=6 years old? No under the Authority and Practice Standard. Refer to GP.' and Yes/No branch labels appear detached from boxes.
open_questions.why_unclear: Step order and on_fail assignments were inferred from the diagram layout; branch wording transcribed verbatim. Confidence marked medium on PW-1-S3.

open_questions.topic: Dose, frequency, strength and duration per approved medicine not printed
open_questions.observed: Approved Medicines are listed as 'Fluticasone furoate (intranasal formulation)', 'Olopatadine with mometasone (intranasal formulation)', 'Olopatadine 0.1% (eye drops)' - only Olopatadine has a printed strength; no dose, frequency or duration per administration appears anywhere in the document (deferred to Therapeutic Guidelines).
open_questions.why_unclear: dose, frequency, duration and strength fields left empty rather than invented.

open_questions.topic: Document does not identify which approved medicines are intranasal corticosteroids
open_questions.observed: Statements about intranasal corticosteroids (expect relief within 1-2 weeks; clinical review 4 weeks after initiation; 'mainstay of treatment' for nonallergic rhinitis) are not mapped to named approved medicines in the document.
open_questions.why_unclear: The 1-2 week and 4-week review rules were not attached to specific treatment rows to avoid inventing a drug-level classification; they are recorded as protocol statements in notes and in pathway steps.

open_questions.observed: Three approved medicines listed with no ranking or sequencing; pharmacotherapy is directed to the Therapeutic Guidelines.
open_questions.why_unclear: first_line set to false for all treatments because the document does not designate a first-line agent.

open_questions.topic: Requirement without a stated failure action (otoscope)
open_questions.observed: 'Pharmacist must have an otoscope to complete a full examination' (PW-2-S2 gate) - the document does not say what to do if an otoscope is unavailable.
open_questions.why_unclear: Gate on_fail recorded as 'unclear' per spec; local policy needed.

open_questions.topic: Branch actions not stated for several follow-up gates
open_questions.observed: PW-4-S2 uses on_fail 'unclear' (no stated action if no intranasal corticosteroid was initiated); PW-4-S1/S3 on_fail branches link the mild-symptom and 4-week non-response bullets, which are adjacent bullets rather than an explicit diagram branch.
open_questions.why_unclear: The follow-up section is prose, not a flowchart; branch order was inferred from bullet sequence. Confidence medium on PW-4-S1 and PW-4-S3.

open_questions.topic: 4-week supply cap versus 4-week review and further supply
open_questions.observed: 'Pharmacists can supply up to 4 weeks of therapy before referring patient to a medical practitioner.' (p4) alongside clinical review at 4 weeks and 'continue treatment with the minimum effective regimen' after symptoms resolve (p8-10).
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not state whether further supply beyond 4 weeks is permitted after review, or whether the 4-week cap is per course/consultation.

open_questions.observed: referral.routine quotes are from pages 4-6, urgent quotes from pages 5-6, emergency from pages 3 and 5.
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec requires one shared provenance object for the referral block using the first page; page range recorded here.

open_questions.observed: TGA reporting and notification of the patient's usual medical practitioner wording is on page 2; My Health Record upload requirement is on page 8 (repeated page 10).
open_questions.why_unclear: Shared provenance uses the first page (2) per spec; range recorded here.

open_questions.topic: Referral criteria lists stated as not exhaustive
open_questions.observed: 'Note that these are not exhaustive lists.' and 'Pharmacists must apply clinical judgement and refer any patient considered appropriate for medical care for any reason.'
open_questions.why_unclear: The exclusion/red-flag lists cannot be treated as complete; the engine must allow pharmacist-initiated referral for any reason.

open_questions.observed: 'The patient is taking a medicine prescribe by another health practitioner that can cause or exacerbate rhinitis' (likely 'prescribed').
open_questions.why_unclear: Transcribed verbatim as printed; interpretation flagged for confirmation rather than silently corrected.

open_questions.observed: Page 9 section heading reads 'ALLERGIC RHINTIS' (missing initial 'I'), and 'K. CLINICAL DOCUMENATION AND COMMUNICATION' is spelled 'DOCUMENTATION' in the contents but 'DOCUMENATION' on page 1.
open_questions.why_unclear: Headings transcribed as printed for section_heading provenance; noted so downstream consumers do not treat these as typos in extraction.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Verify the current NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026) Approved Medicines list and any subsequent amendments before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The Approved Medicines list is held in an external Authority document not included in this protocol PDF.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm each pharmacist using the module has completed the training requirements detailed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026) and holds general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Training requirements are detailed in an external document; pharmacist authorisation to practise under the standard must be verified locally.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local process for TGA adverse event reporting via https://aems.tga.gov.au/ and notification of the patient's usual medical practitioner.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Reporting is directed to be done 'via the usual processes', which is left to local policy.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm consent record-sharing within a week of consultation and secure digital record retention (minimum seven (7) years) arrangements.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Documentation, storage and sharing arrangements depend on local pharmacy systems and policy.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm My Health Record upload workflow and patient opt-out handling for each supply.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Upload requirement is stated but the operational process is left to the pharmacy's local workflow.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm otoscope availability/equipment standard for full examination in each participating pharmacy.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Document makes an otoscope mandatory for a full examination but does not state the consequence of unavailability.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the current status of restricted supplies: 'Montelukast ... supply is not currently permitted', anti-inflammatory eye drops not permitted (medical specialist advice only), vasoconstrictor eye drops not indicated.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: 'Not currently permitted' hedges to the current Authority position and must be re-checked against the Authority in force at go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local policy on exercising professional discretion and judgement when applying the Practice Standard.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The standard explicitly defers to pharmacist judgement and consultation with the patient, which is a local policy/governance decision.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm whether supply may continue beyond 4 weeks after clinical review, and how the 4-week cap interacts with the 4-week intranasal corticosteroid review.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document states a 4-week supply limit before referral and a 4-week review point but does not state the rule for further supply.
